It is [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md)'s judgment-valued special case with the converse added: [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) says a partition sufficient for one target need not be for another, and this says which partitions serve a deterministic judgment, those whose fibres lie inside its level sets, so the coarsest is the judgment's own partition. The sharp edge: it says when a description keeps a judgment, never whether the judgment is right. A21's probabilistic and causal versions are recorded in the body, not claimed. | Active |
| [CLAIM-351](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-351.md) v3 | Zero aggregate gradient is not reconciliation | A33 §5 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "Zero aggregate gradient does not imply absence of frustrated demands." With L₁ = (θ − 1)² and L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0 ([CASE-115](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-115.md)), the equal-weight gradient is zero and the aggregate is at its global minimum, while each loss is 1 and wants the opposite move. In general a vanishing positive combination of gradients is either every gradient zero or a certificate that no update improves them all, and the scalar cannot tell which. The sharp edge: it is a fact about a weighted sum, not about what a monitor reading it represents. A29's "the unity of the distress signal need not arise from the unity of the underlying causes" is the interpretive reading, kept apart in the body. | Active |

His process aspect is in part what will-organization models: whether the agent's own governance selected the outcome. Read first-hand in [NOTE-263](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-263.md) (Sen's lecture) and [NOTE-259](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-259.md) (Robeyns). The sharp edge: reachable states are not capabilities, and an efficacious governance is not a fair or legitimate process. | Active |

| [CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md) v4 | Frustration residual has a simplex dual | A34 §4 and A35 §3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, checked. The residual is the smallest worst-case shortfall of the declared local improvements ε_i over updates of size at most r. Minimax for the bilinear problem on two compact convex sets gives the dual over the simplex, so Φ_r > 0 exactly when some λ certifies that no update meets all demands (A34's form). Governance regret Γ is the gap between an actual admissible update's shortfall and Φ_r, and is never negative. For L₁ = (θ − 1)², L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0, Φ_r = ε for every r. The sharp edge: per A37 it is a cardinal refinement of the ordinal fact ([CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)), and its magnitude depends on units (A36 §2D). | Active |
| [CLAIM-366](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-366.md) v3 | Shared descent survives reparameterization | A35 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, at the owner's U35 "double click" on whether functionally equivalent parameterizations give equivalent frustration diagnoses. A Euclidean inner product does: g₁ = (1, 1), g₂ = (1, −½) have product ½, and under θ = diag(½, 2)ψ their transforms have −7/4, while d = (−1, 0) lowers both throughout. | [CLAIM-369](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-369.md) v5 | Lotka–Volterra is gradient flow on selection | From a synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18 (workbench entry of that date), checked here and given a proof. When competition between components is mediated by shared resources with feature or niche vectors u_i, so that A = UᵀU and r = Uᵀb − c, the Lotka–Volterra dynamics are ṅ_i = −n_i ∂_i L with L(n) = ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn: entropic mirror descent on the positive orthant. A rare component's invasion fitness is −∂_i L, the value of adding that feature, and uninvadable equilibria are the KKT points of the convex program. The sharp edge: the identity needs a shared scalar objective, and it fails for asymmetric interactions or processes with competing objectives, which is where an organization stops being an optimizer. Mehta et al. (2019) and Marsland, Cui and Mehta (2020) give the general duality for consumer–resource models. | Active |

([LIT-249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-249.md)) reach the Hilbert– Schmidt property from a uniform bound, which is stronger. Here the condition is exact: Hilbert–Schmidt if and only if finite χ². It says nothing about what trained features span. | Active |

| [CLAIM-372](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-372.md) | Contextual fraction is Lipschitz in the table | The record's own derivation, from the linear programme of Abramsky, Barbosa and Mansfield ([LIT-265](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-265.md), Eq. 3), which [THEORY-165](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-165.md) holds. The non-contextual fraction is the minimum of the dual objective over finitely many vertices, so it is concave and piecewise linear in the probability table, and the contextual fraction is Lipschitz in it. The constant is the largest ℓ₁ norm of a dual vertex, which depends only on the scenario and is not bounded here. Nothing here crosses scenarios or applies to signalling data. | Active |

[ARG-006](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-006.md) is the exact case. It says nothing about whether the defects can be identified from data ([CLAIM-253](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-253.md)), or what bounds an observed order effect ([CLAIM-231](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-231.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-374](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-374.md) | CbD and sheaf criterion agree when consistent | The record's derivation of what [NOTE-600](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-600.md) marks as its own inference. In a consistently connected system, every observable has one distribution in all the contexts that contain it. Then each connection's maximal coupling makes its copies equal with probability 1 ([LIT-777](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-777.md), Theorem 3.3), so a maximally connected coupling is a joint law of one variable per observable, which is a global section in Abramsky and Brandenburger's sense ([LIT-016](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-016.md), [THEORY-012](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-012.md)). Conversely, a global section gives such a coupling. The two criteria come apart only when marginals shift with context. | Active |

If the collective decision is the authority-weighted mean of the operators' policies, then granting influence to an ally whose policy is nearer one's own than the decision is moves the decision strictly toward one's policy. So the reward for realized policy, and not for held authority, pays for delegating. It does not say operators behave so, or that any rule beyond one hop keeps both conditions. | Active |
| [CLAIM-376](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-376.md) v2 | Instantaneously stable yet positive Lyapunov | The case [THEORY-724](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-724.md)'s source asserts and does not show. If A(t) has first Lyapunov exponent λ > 0, the propagator of A(t) − δI is e^(−δt)Φ(t), so its exponent is exactly λ − δ, while every eigenvalue of every A(t) moves left by δ. Applied to the undamped oscillator switching ω between 0.5 and 3 every unit of time: λ = 0.1955, and with δ = 0.1 the system is stable at every instant, with eigenvalues −0.1 ± 3i and −0.1 ± 0.5i, and has exponent 0.0955. | Active |
| [CLAIM-377](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-377.md) | Fisher equals Gauss–Newton and empirical NTK | [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s Step 1, stated as the record's own and proved. Through the SVD J = UΣVᵀ, JᵀJ and JJᵀ share the non-zero eigenvalues σ_i² with equal multiplicities, and Jᵀu/σ is the eigenvector of JᵀJ for a unit eigenvector u of JJᵀ. Under y \| x ~ N(f(x; θ), β⁻¹), the expected outer product of the score is β∇f∇fᵀ, which summed over inputs is βJᵀJ, the Gauss–Newton matrix. "Fisher" means the model's Fisher, not the empirical Fisher of observed residuals. It holds at every width, in every regime and on any data. It says nothing about what the spectrum looks like, which is [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s. | Active |
| [CLAIM-378](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-378.md) v2 | Linear-invariant similarity sees column space | The generalization of [THEORY-236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-236.md)'s theorem. If col(X) = col(Y), write X = BC and Y = BD with B a basis of the common column space and C, D of full row rank, extend C and D to invertible matrices, and the quotient maps X onto Y. Since XA always has the column space of X, the GL(p) orbits are exactly the sets of n × p matrices sharing a column space. Theorem 1 is the case of column space ℝⁿ. Column-centred matrices of rank n − 1 all have column space 1^⊥, so an invariant index cannot tell them apart either. | Active |
| [CLAIM-379](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-379.md) v2 | Ridge readouts see representations up to rotation | The proved core of [CLAIM-269](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-269.md). What a regularized linear readout decodes is a function of K_X = X G⁻¹ Xᵀ/M, with G = aC_X + bI ([THEORY-008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)). For b > 0, K_X and the Gram matrix XXᵀ determine each other, by a monotone map on the shared eigenvalues; and equal Gram matrices mean an orthogonal transformation ([CLAIM-290](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-290.md), [THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)). For b = 0, K_X is the projection onto the column space, which fixes X only up to an invertible linear map, as for a softmax layer ([THEORY-723](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md)). | Active |

Define D⁺_Q(U → V; π) = sup over q in Q of [r_q,π(V) − r_q,π(U)]⁺, with losses in [0, 1] and a stated prior. A garbling never gains. The term is directed. A86's D_Q is its symmetrization. And with every finite problem and prior, it vanishes exactly when V is at least as informative as U, by Blackwell's Theorem 6 ([THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md)). It does not cover outcome spaces that are not finite, or say this is the right decision term. | Active |
| [CLAIM-381](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-381.md) | Constant outcome kernels need item-blind readers | The derivational core of [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md). Over a finite class of items, the target term is the readers' response averaged over a procedure's output, and one outcome kernel family is fixed across the items. Then a constant kernel fits only target responses that carry no information about the item. An exact fit is a garbling, with the item as the common parameter. And Le Cam's deficiency between the two finite tables is one linear programme. Its restriction to finitely many decision problems is a finite computation. It does not say the measure is informative, which is [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md)'s empirical question. | Active |
| [CLAIM-382](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-382.md) v2 | Autoencoder representations are rotation-invariant | [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s symmetry argument, stated as the record's own and proved. Transform the parameters by orthogonal maps Q_l of the hidden spaces that commute with the activation. The network then computes Q_l h_l and the same output, so the loss is invariant. Gradient steps commute with the transformation, and an i.i.d. Gaussian initialisation is invariant under it, so the law of the trained representations is too. For radial activations this is all of O(n), and no basis is privileged in law. For elementwise ones it is a finite group, so the axes may be privileged. Whether they are, and how strongly, is [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s empirical content. The argument needs an orthogonally equivariant optimiser, and fails for Adam. | Active |
| [CLAIM-383](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-383.md) v3 | Shear flows have transient growth at least cR | [THEORY-304](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-304.md)'s scalings as lower bounds, derived. At streamwise wavenumber zero, the cross-stream velocities obey an R-independent Stokes problem in the time t/R. They force the streamwise velocity through −U′v, so the streamwise response is R times an R-independent field. In the energy norm this gives transient growth at least cR, and in the steady forced problem a resolvent norm at least cR². Through pseudospectra, a perturbation of norm O(R⁻²) then moves an eigenvalue into the unstable half-plane wherever the flow is eigenvalue-stable. The sharp constants, and that the growth is no more than order R, come from the computation and are not here. | Active |

| [CLAIM-452](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-452.md) v2 | Authority shares identifiable from contexts | When an organization's response in context c is p_π(·\|c) = Σᵢ πᵢ pᵢ(·\|c), the mixture [CLAIM-444](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-444.md) reduces the replicator model to, which probe contexts reveal its authority shares π? Concatenating a path from x to y with one from y to z has peak max(d(x, y), d(y, z)), so d(x, z) ≤ max(d(x, y), d(y, z)): d is an extended pseudo-ultrametric (distinct states joined at no cost are at distance 0, unjoined ones at ∞; it is an ultrametric only when every pair of distinct states is separated by a positive cost). Hence at each budget b, "x and y can be turned into one another within b" is an equivalence relation, its classes are the components of the budget-b move graph, and as b grows the classes only merge, forming one dendrogram, the merge tree of zero-dimensional sublevel persistence (Mirth et al.). Under additive costs d is a metric and budgeted identification is intransitive in general. So which resource semantics governs a system decides whether "the same thing, within budget" sorts its configurations into a hierarchy of kinds at all. Investing raises survival over 40 periods only above a buffer of 4 when the payoff comes after 1 period, rising to 5, 6, 9 and 14 at delays of 4, 9, 16 and 25. Below it, declining is right. Implication does not remove the linear directions. Every attribute is read out exactly, by an affine map, from the full-rank spectral embedding, and the recovered incidence and its concept lattice equal the generating ones. What implication changes is the spectrum. On a balanced b-ary tree, the eigenvectors are branch contrasts rather than one per attribute. A branching at depth ℓ gives eigenvalue μ_ℓ = w Σ_{ℓ′>ℓ} λ_ℓ′ b^(D−ℓ′), with multiplicity (b−1)bˡ, and these fall strictly with depth for any positive strengths. So a rank-(b^K − 1) embedding reads out exactly the attributes of depth at most K. Below the cut, each attribute's readout is the same constant on every descendant of its depth-K ancestor, so siblings merge. Along a tree, PMI additivity is therefore the same thing as piecewise constancy on the finest groups: it has content only where attributes cross-cut, as in analogy families. | [CLAIM-1046](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1046.md) v2 | Probe partitions are not the decomposition lattice | A15 §2 says "the lattice of all partitions of Ω is generally much larger than the set of partitions realizable by our affordable probes", and that the probe lattice "is a structure of which distinctions our methods support", not of selves. For fixed configurations Ω and fixed response laws, let π(Q) be the partition of Ω into classes no probe in Q separates. Then π(Q1 ∪ Q2) is the meet (common refinement) of π(Q1) and π(Q2), while π(Q1 ∩ Q2) is at least as coarse as their join and can be strictly coarser. So π is order-reversing and meet-preserving, its image is a meet-closed part of the partition lattice and need not be a sublattice, and with m probes it has at most 2^m members, against Bell(\|Ω\|) partitions (32 against 115,975 for m = 5 and \|Ω\| = 10). Checked with python3 -I on 3,000 random probe systems (no union failed; the intersection was strictly coarser than the join in 100) and on an explicit case.
